raised.claim: Adding any beer ID bypasses the prohibition on whole-class scopes.
raised.why_it_breaks: A proposal with beer_ids: [1] and where: [{col: 'review_class', op: '=', value: 'matcher_bug'}] passes legality. Because rowSatisfiesScope combines the cohort and predicate with OR, every future matcher_bug row also satisfies this scope, recreating the whole-class dumping ground the guard is intended to prohibit.

raised.claim: Attachments to newly proposed issues never undergo the scope compatibility check.
raised.why_it_breaks: A new issue scoped to candidates_count > 0 with an empty beer_ids array is legal, but a verdict attaching a zero-candidate row to its key is still accepted and persisted. The same attachment would be rejected if the issue already existed.

raised.claim: The saturation guard does not count attachments already accepted in the current plan.
raised.why_it_breaks: If an issue starts with 11 post-creation rows and the batch contains 50 compatible verdicts targeting it, all 50 compare against the unchanged value 11 and pass. The resulting comment increases the issue to 61 rows despite the limit of 12.

raised.quote:
const body = `${issue.body}\n\n${renderScopeBlock(issue.scope)}`;
        const number = await github.createIssue({ title: issue.title, body, labels: issue.labels });
raised.claim: Model-authored issue prose can override the authoritative structured scope.
raised.why_it_breaks: The unrestricted issue.body can contain its own valid triage-scope block before the appended block. On the next run, parseScopeBlock takes the first match, so a body containing a broad or different scope silently overrides the structured scope that passed the proposal guard. An earlier malformed block instead makes the issue unscoped.

raised.claim: An empty probe permits an absence verdict even when the other probe returned contradictory positive evidence.
raised.why_it_breaks: For a beer whose scraped brewery is misspelled, the brewery-only probe can return an empty string while the name-only probe returns the actual beer. This OR condition still accepts not_on_untappd, preserving the false absence classification and blocking the paid fallback despite a successful probe.

raised.claim: Guard counters are not logged when the model supplies a verdict for every row, even if the guards reject every verdict.
raised.why_it_breaks: covered counts IDs in analysis.verdicts before guard rejection. If all 50 rows receive scope-violating verdicts, covered remains 50 and this warning never runs. The rows can repeat tomorrow without the per-guard diagnostics promised for precisely this failure mode; absence downgrades are likewise invisible when coverage is complete.

raised.claim: Newly downgraded absence verdicts are reported as wontfix in the job outcome.
raised.why_it_breaks: A not_on_untappd verdict without a probe now enters plan.quiet as matcher_bug. The job's quiet execution loop increments outcome.wontfix for every class other than not_on_untappd, so a batch of these recoverable downgrades is advertised in the persisted digest as wontfix even though the database stores matcher_bug.

raised.claim: The newly persisted issue link is not cleared when a failure is reopened for triage.
raised.why_it_breaks: After a row is linked to issue 347, recordEnrichFailure can receive a candidates_count transition from positive to zero. Its reset clears review_class, review_note and reviewed_at but leaves the new issue_number untouched. The supposedly authoritative link then still associates an untriaged, potentially scope-incompatible row with issue 347 until another verdict is successfully applied.

raised.claim: The post-creation comparison orders timestamp strings rather than instants, despite GitHub and the job using different timestamp precision.
raised.why_it_breaks: GitHub created_at uses a value such as 2026-08-14T06:00:00Z, while reviewed_at is written with milliseconds. A review at 2026-08-14T06:00:00.500Z is later chronologically but compares smaller lexicographically because '.' sorts before 'Z', so it is omitted from the saturation count. Other accepted ISO offset representations can cause larger discrepancies.

raised.claim: Appending scopes after unrestricted prose can hide the routing constraints from subsequent triage prompts.
raised.why_it_breaks: For an issue with at least 2,000 characters of model-authored prose, buildTriagePrompt truncates the body before the appended scope. The deterministic guard still reads the full scope, but the model deciding where to attach rows cannot see it, allowing repeated incompatible proposals and skipped rows without ever presenting the missing constraint to the model.

raised.claim: The strict tool schema accepts scope terms that the required Zod scope schema rejects.
raised.why_it_breaks: A tool response containing {col: 'candidates_count', op: '>', value: '0'} or an unsupported operator satisfies this JSON schema but fails ScopeTermSchema. Because scope validation is part of AnalysisSchema, one such proposal invalidates the entire analysis, including otherwise usable verdicts, rather than being handled by the deterministic illegal-scope guard.

raised.quote:
export const V23_BACKFILL_SQL = `
  UPDATE enrich_failures
     SET issue_number = CAST(substr(review_note, instr(review_note, '→ #') + 3) AS INTEGER)
   WHERE review_note LIKE '%→ #%'
     AND CAST(substr(review_note, instr(review_note, '→ #') + 3) AS INTEGER) > 0;
raised.claim: The migration treats the first arrow reference anywhere in a free-text note as the authoritative issue link.
raised.why_it_breaks: A legacy note such as 'previous routing → #347; corrected → #405' is backfilled as issue 347 rather than its final routing destination 405. Likewise, an arrow reference inside the model's review_note takes precedence over the actual suffix appended by the job, producing an incorrect persisted link and saturation count.
